title: Doorstep launch budget
scratchpad:
Doorstep: Ines asks 4,500 first month, approved
SEPARATE line from Atlas, monthly report
video + 2 trade newsletters + customer story, no podcast
no dates yet
segments: Short one today. Ines wants to talk about money for marketing the add-ons, Doorstep in particular, before the Atlas noise takes over everyone's calendar.
Right. Doorstep is the one homeowners actually see, so it's the one worth marketing. Stockroom sells itself on sales calls.
I'm asking for four thousand five hundred dollars for the first month of Doorstep launch spend.
Is that on top of the Atlas money, or carved out of it?
On top. The Atlas cap stays exactly where it is, and I'm not touching it. This would be a separate line in next quarter's plan.
Then I want it as its own line with its own report. I don't want the two budgets blurring together in anyone's head.
Fine with me. I'd rather keep them apart anyway, so we can tell which one worked.
Three things. A short video of a homeowner getting the tracking link, an ad in two trade newsletters, and a customer story with one of our plumbing customers.
No. The podcast audience is dispatch managers, and they'll have just heard all about Atlas. For Doorstep I want to reach the business owners instead.
The video, at about half. The newsletters are most of the rest, and the customer story is mostly our own time.
And the newsletters? Which ones, and do we know anything about who actually reads them?
Two trade newsletters for plumbing and heating businesses. Both publish their readership, and most readers own or run a small shop.
Which customer for the story? It needs to be someone whose customers would actually notice the tracking link.
Ferrybank Plumbing. Their owner already sends homeowners a text with a photo of the technician, by hand, every single morning.
That's perfect. Doorstep does exactly what he's doing by hand, so the story writes itself.
Okay. I can approve four thousand five hundred for the first month, as a separate line, with a monthly spend report.
Good. Marcus, is there anything you need from Ines for the product page?
Just the video, once it exists. I'd like it on the Doorstep page instead of a static screenshot.
I'll own all three pieces. Marcus gets the video first.
And measurement? How do we know if it worked?
Doorstep Pay sign-ups in the first month, and how many accounts switch the tracking link on.
Keep it to those two. I don't want a dashboard of twenty vanity numbers that nobody reads.
Can the video be short enough to use in the app as well? A thirty second version would work on the Doorstep settings screen.
I'll ask for two cuts, a full one for the page and a thirty second one for the app. It barely changes the cost.
If the two cuts push the video over half the money, tell me before you sign anything with the agency.
One thing we're not doing today is picking dates for any of this. Ines, plan the pieces now, and we'll schedule them closer to the time.
Works for me. I'd rather not commit to dates while Atlas is still taking up everyone's week.

items.text: Doorstep launch spend approved at $4,500 for the first month, as a separate line from the Atlas budget, with a monthly spend report
Produce the Doorstep video, two trade newsletter ads and the Ferrybank Plumbing customer story
